record.original_question: Develop a standard notation for solutions of the Painlevé equations that can distinguish the many analytically different families of Painlevé transcendents, including general two-parameter transcendental solutions, special-function solutions, rational solutions, and distinguished pole-free or sectorially pole-free families such as Ablowitz–Segur, Hastings–McLeod, tronquée, and tri-tronquée solutions.

evidence.quote: However, for nonlinear equations such as the Painlev´e equations, the issue of notation is not as simple as there are numerous completely different solutions. Although second-order equations, there don’t exist two "representative solutions". What is needed is some agreed notation for the Painlev´e transcendents.
Open Problem 3.1. Develop a notation for the Painlev´e transcendents which takes into account the wide variety of solutions the Painlev´e equations have.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a community-convention/notation question. No standardized notation distinguishing all analytic classes of Painlevé transcendents (general, special-function, rational, tronquée, tri-tronquée, Hastings–McLeod, Ablowitz–Segur, etc.) has been adopted. The DLMF Chapter 32 and standard monographs treat solution families case-by-case without a unified naming scheme, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: DLMF: Chapter 32 Painlevé Transcendents
status_evidence.snippet: DLMF describes Painlevé transcendents family-by-family with ad hoc notation for special solutions rather than a unified naming convention.
status_evidence.claim: No standardized cross-equation notation distinguishing all analytic classes is in place in the authoritative reference.

status_evidence.title: Painlevé transcendents - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Different distinguished solutions (Hastings-McLeod, tronquée, tri-tronquée, Ablowitz-Segur) are described in prose with disparate ad hoc names.
status_evidence.claim: Standard exposition uses non-uniform, historically based names rather than a systematic notation.
